meanings.note: Appartenir à quelqu'un. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to belong'.

examples.text: Ton corps t'appartient. On ne possède pas quelqu'un.
examples.trans: Your body belongs to you. You do not own someone.

meanings.note: For people use 'amener'. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to bring'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'apporté').

examples.text: J'ai apporté cinq exemplaires des contrats.
examples.trans: I've brought five copies of the contracts.

examples.text: Il m'apportait un cadeau et passait du temps avec moi.
examples.trans: He would bring me a gift and spend time with me.

meanings.note: Un grand artiste = a great artist. Masculine noun ('le artiste', plural 'les artistes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'artist'.

examples.text: Je travaille avec des artistes photographes.

meanings.note: Core French preposition meaning 'with', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.

meanings.note: C'est du passé = it's in the past. Masculine noun ('le passé', plural 'les passés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'past'.

examples.trans: It's in the past. I've turned the page.

meanings.note: Avoir peur de = to be afraid of. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'fear'.

examples.text: Elle a peur de rater quelque chose.

meanings.note: With ne: je n'en peux plus. Invariable French adverb meaning 'no more'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

meanings.note: Un rôle précieux = a precious role. French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots. Prefix 'pré-' (from Latin 'prae-') means 'before, in advance'.

examples.trans: These roles are precious for his age.

meanings.note: Prêt à + infinitive = ready to. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'ready'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
